analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date and adds a paragraph at head lines 1287-1300. No executable code or security controls change. Because that added paragraph falls outside the supplied head units (1612-2427), I examined it only through the patch excerpt; the units themselves contain only unchanged surrounding documentation.

The new paragraph describes ChunkBatcher.enqueue behavior: it drops a frame immediately if no session sink is bound, with the sink check made on the serial queue at closure-run time. It also notes that SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects, so a late frame from an old request could pass the sink check after a replacement session binds. The doc says plainly that this does not enforce request-to-session identity. This is relevant to TB-002, T-008 and T-053-style stale-session concerns. It is an observation documented by the PR, not a regression introduced by it. The supplied evidence does not show the code, so I cannot confirm whether frames are encrypted per-request, whether the coordinator rejects frames for unknown or cancelled requests, or whether ProviderLoop+Cancellation.swift fully drains in-flight work before rebind. A cross-request frame leak looks mitigated only if each frame is E2E-encrypted to its request's session key and carries a request_id the coordinator validates. That is outside the supplied evidence.

The remaining units cover MTP, sampling, SSD prefix cache references, MiMo and similar areas. They are unchanged context, and the T-041 definition is consistent with them. The threat model may warrant a note that the provider does not bind a chunk to its session at the transport layer. That is a documentation question, not a finding. No findings are raised.
